bio: I am a Senior Lecturer at the **School of Computer Science** at [The Academic College of Tel Aviv-Yaffo (MTA)](https://www.mta.ac.il/en), where I head the graduate program, and a Research Scientist in the AI and Language group at [IBM Research](https://research.ibm.com). My research lies in **natural language processing** and **machine learning**, with a strong interest in how language reflects the people who use it.

My recent work focuses on the **reliability and robustness of large language models and agentic systems**, and on **computational social science**: political polarization, gender and language, and personality in text. Earlier, I studied **multilingualism**: translationese, native-language effects on second-language use, and code-switching.

Before joining MTA, I was a postdoctoral fellow in the [Computational Linguistics group](https://www.cs.toronto.edu/compling/) at the University of Toronto, hosted by Prof. Suzanne Stevenson. I received my Ph.D. in Computer Science from the University of Haifa (advisor: Prof. Shuly Wintner), and my M.Sc. and B.Sc. (both cum laude) from the Technion. At IBM Research, I was part of the [Project Debater](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03215-w) team.
